message.reasoning:
I need to write JUnit 4 tests for the WritableObjectId class using Mockito to mock dependencies, so I'm analyzing the branch conditions in the writeAsId logic based on combinations of id nullness, idWritten, and alwaysAsId flags.

For the true branch, I'm also tracking whether canWriteObjectId leads to writeObjectRef versus serializer.serialize, then moving to generateId and writeAsField which similarly branch on canWriteObjectId and whether name is null.

I'll need to mock JsonGenerator, SerializerProvider, ObjectIdWriter, ObjectIdGenerator, JsonSerializer, and SerializableString, and I'm inferring the likely field structure of ObjectIdWriter (alwaysAsId, serializer, propertyName) since the full source isn't given.

Recalling more of the actual Jackson class, it has final fields for idType, generator, propertyName, serializer, and alwaysAsId, and a protected constructor taking these values along with an ObjectIdGenerator.

Since the constructor is protected, tests would need to use the static factory method forBeanProperty, or place the test in the same package to access the protected constructor directly since protected includes package-level access in Java.

So I'll place the test in that package and construct ObjectIdWriter directly with the protected constructor, passing null for the JavaType and generator fields since they aren't used in writeAsId/writeAsField -- only alwaysAsId, serializer, and propertyName matter for those methods.

Now I'm sketching out the test cases: verifying writeAsId returns false when id is null, false when id isn't written and alwaysAsId is false, true when the id is written and canWriteObjectId succeeds, true when alwaysAsId is set and the serializer path is used instead, plus a test confirming generateId invokes the generator and stores the result.

I'm also planning writeAsField tests -- checking it writes the object id and flips idWritten to true when canWriteObjectId succeeds, otherwise falls back to writing the field name and serializing when a name exists, or does nothing extra when the name is null. I note that writeAsId itself never touches idWritten, only writeAsField does, and I'm setting up mocks for the generic serializer and object id generator to support these cases.

I mock out the remaining collaborators -- SerializableString, JsonGenerator, SerializerProvider -- and use null for JavaType since it's unused in these paths. I construct an ObjectIdWriter with alwaysAsId true using these mocks, then plan to verify the serializer's serialize method gets invoked via Mockito in the writeAsId else-branch test before finalizing the full test class.
